blogs.title: Collecting Penalties From the Top: The 8th Circuit’s Confirmation That Only the Commissioner Can Seek Wage‑Law Penalties
blogs.description: The Court’s ruling clarifies that employees can never personally collect statutory penalties under the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act (and by extension the MFLSA and MWTA). In this post, we break down the statutory construction that places enforcement in the hands of the Commissioner, how this limits employee standing, and why the decision matters for wage‑law litigants who seek punitive redress.

blogs.title: Mootness, Standing, and the Future of Wage Penalties: Lessons from Cohen v. Consilio
blogs.description: When a company’s policy is altered, can a plaintiff still demand penalties? This analysis examines the 8th Circuit’s vacating of the MFLSA penalty claim, the mootness reasoning under Friends of the Earth, and the delicate line between ‘no continuing injury’ and ‘no continuing interest.’ We explain how the Court navigated jurisdiction concerns and set a precedent for future wage‑law litigation.

blogs.title: No Penalties, No Problem? Why Minnesota’s Wage Theft Act Provides No Enforcement Remedy in Wage‑Laws Cases
blogs.description: Minnesota’s Wage Theft Act includes a notice‑and‑correct window but no statutory penalties. In Cohen v. Consilio, the Court dismissed the MWTA claim for this reason. We discuss statutory interpretation of § 181.032, the difference between injunctions and penalties, and the impact on employees who rely on punitive damages to deter wrongful conduct.

blogs.title: Policy Changes in the Midst of Litigation: How Consilio's New Overtime Premium Rule Undermined Cohen’s Claims
blogs.description: Employers can shift overtime policies, but what does that do to current claims? The Court assessed the effect of Consilio’s new ‘premium overtime’ rule on Cohen’s remedy. This post examines the interplay between policy modifications, settlement negotiations, class‑action viability, and offers guidance to employers on the frontiers of compliance, settlement, and ongoing litigation.
